complete_rollback_adversary.description: actual later authority revoked the artifact, but repository authority and remembered policy/revocation state are fully rewound so floor, tombstone, family incarnation and current-policy reverify all appear pre-revocation
complete_rollback_adversary.interpretation: Bloom false positives happen to block half the equal-weight rollback slice but are not an authority proof. No repository-local mechanism in this model can distinguish a world that never advanced from one that advanced and was completely rolled back.

interpretation.prefix_vs_sparse: A monotonic family epoch floor compactly represents prefix revocation but misses sparse revocations; an exact hash tombstone set represents sparse revocation but misses prefix revocation unless every old hash is materialized. Their conjunction covers both within the stated current-state invariants.
interpretation.bloom_tradeoff: Replacing the sparse exact set with an authoritative Bloom filter can preserve safety under the ideal no-false-negative construction but introduces false positive exclusions. It is therefore an availability/storage tradeoff, not a stronger proof.
interpretation.reverify: When an old artifact is blocked, current deterministic local re-verification can mint a new acceptance identity under the current policy hash and reduces false exclusions without resurrecting the revoked old acceptance.
interpretation.family_recreate: Policy-family delete/recreate requires an incarnation-sensitive family identity. Reusing only the family name can let old artifacts cross into a new policy family.
interpretation.rollback_boundary: Complete rollback of repository authority plus remembered local state remains indistinguishable from a world that never advanced. Revocation floors, tombstones, Bloom filters and current-policy reverify all inherit this authority-domain boundary.

unresolved_children: no repository-local anti-rollback witness survives complete rollback of repository authority plus all remembered own state
a compact exact-hash grandfather/revocation registry is not currently exposed by frozen control/config
family-incarnation migration across delete/recreate requires current authority metadata; family name alone is insufficient
exact_continuation: Next leaf: rollback-domain escape without hosted coordination. Compare user-visible immutable prompt/control facts, Git object reachability/ancestry, branch protection/ruleset observations, local acceptance receipt chains, multiple independent repository refs, and fail-closed no-witness under force-rewind/delete-recreate/full-state-loss. The goal is to determine whether any scheduled-Chat-native zero-quota witness is genuinely outside the repository rollback domain; if none is available, formalize the indistinguishability boundary and select the next independent multi-agent leaf rather than declaring Phase-1 complete.
